title: Unit 01: Book-II Prose Part 1 (The Dying Sun, Scientific Method, Boys Fail)
subject: english-12

questions.question: According to Sir James Jeans in 'The Dying Sun', why is a rare occurrence for a star to come close to another star?

options.A: Stars travel in fixed magnetic orbits that keep them synchronized.
options.B: Space is so immense that a star travels millions of miles without meeting another, like a solitary ship on an ocean.
options.C: Stars possess gravitational repulsions that push oncoming bodies away.
options.D: Most stars are cold and do not radiate gravitational attraction.

questions.explanation: Sir James Jeans compares space to an immense ocean where each star is like a lonely ship traveling hundreds of thousands of miles without encountering another vessel.

questions.question: What created the gigantic tidal wave on the surface of our sun millions of years ago?

options.A: A sudden nuclear explosion within the core of the sun
options.B: The rare close approach of another wandering star in space
options.C: An intense solar eclipse created by planetary conjunction
options.D: The rapid decrease in the rotational momentum of the galaxy

questions.explanation: As the wandering star came closer and closer to the sun, the tidal attraction raised a huge mountain on the sun's surface, which eventually broke into pieces called planets.

questions.question: What fundamental condition is highlighted in 'The Dying Sun' as indispensable for life to exist on a planet?

options.A: Intense solar radiation to trigger atomic ionization
options.B: A moderate temperature zone where substances can exist in a liquid state
options.C: A dense gaseous atmosphere composed primarily of hydrogen and methane
options.D: A completely frozen planetary core with no tectonic activity

questions.explanation: Life requires a narrow temperature belt where it is neither too hot that liquids boil away nor too cold that everything freezes solid.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', Sir James Jeans concludes that life most likely originated in:

options.A: Volcanic craters under high electrical discharges
options.B: Lukewarm oceans and shallow pools of water on Earth
options.C: Meteoritic impacts bringing spores from outer galaxies
options.D: High mountain peaks exposed to cosmic rays

questions.explanation: Jeans describes life starting as simple organisms in lukewarm waters, capable of reproducing before dying, slowly evolving into complex beings.

questions.question: In 'Using the Scientific Method', Darrel Barnard & Lon Edwards note that two centuries ago, city streets were typically:

options.A: Paved with macadam and washed regularly by city sanitation carts
options.B: Unpaved, muddy, and served as dumping grounds for garbage and sewage
options.C: Constructed with underground brick drainage systems
options.D: Disinfected weekly with chlorinated lime solutions

questions.explanation: Streets 200 years ago were narrow, unpaved dirt alleys where household trash, night-soil, and refuse were thrown directly into open gutters.

questions.question: Which deadly water-borne diseases have been virtually eradicated in modern civilized cities through the scientific method?

options.A: Typhoid fever and cholera
options.B: Tuberculosis and scurvy
options.C: Rickets and beriberi
options.D: Influenza and measles

questions.explanation: Clean municipal water pipelines and sewage treatment eliminated widespread epidemics of typhoid fever, cholera, and dysentery.

questions.question: What modern method of food preservation preserves flavor and vitamins while preventing bacterial decay through rapid temperature reduction?

options.A: Excessive pickling with vinegar
options.B: Quick-freezing (deep freezing)
options.C: Smoking over oak wood
options.D: Sun-drying on rooftops

questions.explanation: Quick-freezing stops bacterial enzymatic action while preserving texture, nutritional vitamins, and fresh flavor in vegetables and meats.

questions.question: How does an educated scientific mind handle superstitions such as fear of the number 13 or black cats?

options.A: It rejects beliefs that have no empirical basis in cause-and-effect relationships.
options.B: It observes them secretly just in case luck plays a role.
options.C: It accepts them as ancient psychological wisdom.
options.D: It replaces them with astrological horoscopes.

questions.explanation: A person with a scientific attitude demands proven facts and logical causes before accepting any belief, rejecting baseless folklore and superstition.

questions.question: In 'Why Boys Fail in College', Herbert E. Hawkes identifies the primary cause of failure among boys with adequate academic ability as:

options.A: Lack of nervous vitality and lack of personal ambition
options.B: Inability to sit at a desk and concentrate on the task at hand
options.C: A complete lack of textbooks in college libraries
options.D: Severe university exam cheating penalties

questions.explanation: Hawkes explains that many capable boys fail because they develop nervous fidgeting habits—sharpening pencils, shuffling papers—instead of doing the work.

questions.question: According to Dean Hawkes, why is a boy forced into medicine or engineering by his parents likely to fail?

options.A: His natural aptitudes and genuine interest lie elsewhere, causing chronic lack of motivation.
options.B: Medical and engineering programs refuse students selected by parents.
options.C: His parents refuse to provide tuition fees.
options.D: College faculty actively discourage parental guidance.

questions.explanation: A boy whose heart is in theatrical production or writing will have no enthusiasm for anatomy or calculus, leading to academic paralysis.

questions.question: What type of student does Dean Hawkes describe as 'the bright boy who has never learned what work is'?

options.A: The student who easily passed high school with minimal effort and finds college standards demanding genuine hard labor.
options.B: The student who has attended night school while working full-time.
options.C: The athlete who refuses to attend lecture halls.
options.D: The student who suffers from chronic organic ailments.

questions.explanation: Students who effortlessly sailed through high school without ever studying often experience shock when college requires consistent, disciplined study.

questions.question: What role should college health services play in diagnosing student failure according to Hawkes?

options.A: Expelling sick students to prevent contagion
options.B: Identifying physical handicaps such as defective eyesight, infected tonsils, or glandular disorders that drain energy
options.C: Prescribing sedatives before examinations
options.D: Banning physical sports for low-performing students

questions.explanation: Unsuspected physical defects—such as poor vision, sleeping sickness, or bad teeth—often drain a boy's stamina, which a college physician must address.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', what fraction of the universe is represented by matter as compared to the immense vacuum?

options.A: Almost half of space is packed with matter.
options.B: An unimaginably tiny fraction; total matter is like a grain of sand compared to the world's beaches.
options.C: One-fourth of the universe is dense matter.
options.D: All interstellar space is filled with dense ether.

questions.explanation: The amount of solid matter in the universe is infinitesimal compared to the unfathomable empty reaches of cold space.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', why did the mountain raised on the sun by the wandering star burst into fragments?

options.A: Because the sun's internal pressure exceeded its outer crust threshold.
options.B: Because the star came closer and its gravitational pull exceeded the sun's cohesive strength, tearing the tidal crest off.
options.C: Due to a direct physical collision between the two celestial bodies.
options.D: Because of rapid thermal contraction as the sun cooled down.

questions.explanation: As the wandering star drew nearer, the tidal wave rose so high that its summit detached under overwhelming gravitational attraction, hurling pieces into orbit.

questions.question: What is the primary psychological obstacle for students working their way through college as noted by Hawkes?

options.A: They become snobbish and despise their peers.
options.B: Physical exhaustion from long hours of manual labor leaves them with neither energy nor time for deep academic study.
options.C: They are prohibited from sitting in final examinations.
options.D: They always score the highest grades without effort.

questions.explanation: Working 6 to 8 hours a day for wages leaves students physically depleted, causing them to fall asleep over books or fail exams.

questions.question: In 'Using the Scientific Method', how did our ancestors view natural disasters like famines and plagues?

options.A: As biological imbalances to be corrected by vaccination
options.B: As punishments from angry deities or evil spirits that must be appeased through magical charms
options.C: As inevitable astronomical shifts
options.D: As opportunities for scientific research

questions.explanation: Primitive people attributed disease and crop failure to evil spirits and witchcraft because they lacked scientific knowledge of germs and meteorology.

questions.question: What is the definition of a 'critical attitude' developed through scientific education?

options.A: Finding fault in every person's behavior
options.B: Evaluating claims based on verified evidence rather than hearsay, tradition, or emotional bias
options.C: Criticizing literary masterpieces in academic journals
options.D: Refusing to believe in scientific laws

questions.explanation: A critical, open-minded attitude means suspending judgement until reproducible evidence is available to confirm or deny an assertion.

questions.question: The term 'nervous habits' in Hawkes' essay refers to:

options.A: Severe neurological diseases requiring surgical intervention
options.B: Unconscious displacement activities students use to postpone or avoid intellectual effort
options.C: Compulsive exercise routines before classes
options.D: Smoking cigarettes in the university cafeteria

questions.explanation: Sharpening pencils, pacing the floor, and cleaning desks are subconscious stalling maneuvers to dodge hard mental exertion.

questions.question: Why does life appear so rare and precious in Jeans' cosmic analysis in 'The Dying Sun'?

options.A: Because almost all of space is either intensely hot inside stars or freezing cold in the cosmic vacuum.
options.B: Because radiation from black holes destroys all biological matter.
options.C: Because only Earth possesses gravity in the Milky Way.
options.D: Because oxygen exists only on our moon.

questions.explanation: Stars are gigantic incandescent furnaces where life would burn, and open space is near absolute zero, making hospitable temperature zones extraordinary anomalies.

questions.question: Which word is synonymous with 'superstition' as discussed in 'Using the Scientific Method'?

options.A: Empirical deduction
options.B: Unfounded belief / Irrational dread
options.C: Logical hypothesis
options.D: Systematic verification

questions.explanation: Superstition is an irrational belief arising from ignorance or fear of the unknown, unsupported by factual evidence.

questions.question: What advice does Dean Hawkes give to parents who persistently force an unsuitable career onto their son?

options.A: The college should take legal custody of the student.
options.B: Parents must be told that their boy is living his own life, not his father's, and must follow his innate passion.
options.C: The boy should be expelled until he obeys his parents.
options.D: The father should take the classes alongside his son.

questions.explanation: Hawkes insists that a boy's own talent and passion must govern his career choice rather than a parent's unfulfilled personal ambition.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'infinitesimal' as used in 'The Dying Sun'?

options.A: Microscopic
options.B: Minute
options.C: Colossal / Immense
options.D: Negligible

questions.explanation: 'Infinitesimal' means unimaginably small; its direct antonym is colossal, immense, or gigantic.

questions.question: In 1800, what was the typical life expectancy of a newborn child in European towns compared to modern times?

options.A: Around 70 years due to unpolluted nature
options.B: Less than 35 years due to severe infant mortality and rampant epidemics
options.C: Exactly 50 years
options.D: Around 15 years

questions.explanation: Over half of children died before the age of six, and average life expectancy was under 35 years prior to modern medicine and sanitation.

questions.question: What happens when a college boy is discovered to be a 'loafer' who comes to college purely for social prestige?

options.A: He should be rewarded with leadership positions in fraternities.
options.B: He should be given a cold shower of reality and asked to step aside into the cold world to earn his bread.
options.C: He should be allowed to stay indefinitely as long as tuition is paid.
options.D: He should be transferred to an honors research program.

questions.explanation: Hawkes argues that the lazy boy who drifts aimlessly should be dismissed so that the hard realities of life teach him the value of effort.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly demonstrates the vocabulary word 'disabuse' in the context of student counseling?

options.A: The dean had to disabuse the father of the mistaken notion that his son was born to be an engineer.
options.B: The student disabused his books with highlighter markers.
options.C: The professor disabused the classroom before the lecture.
options.D: The doctor disabused medicine into the syringe.

questions.explanation: 'Disabuse' means to persuade someone that an idea or belief is mistaken or untrue.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', what was the initial state of the planetary bodies after breaking off from the sun?

options.A: Frozen blocks of extraterrestrial ice
options.B: Glowing balls of raging gas that gradually cooled down over aeons
options.C: Solid granite continents covered in rainforests
options.D: Hollow crystalline spheres orbiting the Milky Way

questions.explanation: The planets were originally hot gases that condensed, cooled, and developed crusts over millions of years.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech used in: 'Each star makes its voyage through a universe so spacious that meeting another is like two ships meeting on an empty sea.'

options.A: Hyperbole
options.B: Simile
options.C: Metonymy
options.D: Oxymoron

questions.explanation: The explicit comparison between stars and ships using 'like' is a classic simile.

questions.question: In 'Using the Scientific Method', dehydration is defined as:

options.A: The removal of water/moisture to inhibit microbial multiplication
options.B: Adding liquid nitrogen to preserve enzymes
options.C: Boiling liquids under high atmospheric pressure
options.D: Exposing vegetables to sulfur dioxide gas

questions.explanation: Dehydration extracts water from foods, denying bacteria and moulds the moisture necessary to reproduce.

questions.question: According to Dean Hawkes, why do financial worries affect a student's mental performance?

options.A: Because banks charge high interest rates on credit cards
options.B: Anxiety over tuition bills and food expenses creates chronic psychological stress and distraction
options.C: Because poor students are not permitted into university libraries
options.D: Because textbooks cannot be bought on credit

questions.explanation: Worrying about where the next meal or tuition instalment will come from fractures a student's mental peace and focus.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'feebly' as used in 'The Dying Sun' ('life began in organisms whose vitality consisted feebly of self-reproduction')?

options.A: Vigorously and aggressively
options.B: Faintly, weakly, or with little power
options.C: Rapidly and destructively
options.D: Predictably and mechanically

questions.explanation: 'Feebly' means lacking strength or intensity; in this context, primitive life had very weak, basic biological functions.

questions.question: The scientific method relies upon all of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Careful observation and empirical experimentation
options.B: Blind obedience to traditional superstitions
options.C: Formulating hypotheses and testing deductions
options.D: Drawing conclusions only after verified results

questions.explanation: Blind obedience to tradition without empirical verification is the direct antithesis of the scientific method.

questions.question: In Hawkes' essay, the expression 'to cultivate a habit of work' implies:

options.A: Growing agricultural plants in the university greenhouse
options.B: Systematically training oneself in regular, disciplined intellectual labor
options.C: Working as an apprentice in a machinery workshop
options.D: Doing all homework ten minutes before class

questions.explanation: 'Cultivating a habit of work' means disciplining the mind to sit down, focus, and complete academic tasks steadily every single day.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', our sun is scientifically categorized as:

options.A: An ordinary star of medium size and average temperature
options.B: A colossal supergiant star at the center of the universe
options.C: A dense white dwarf with frozen oceans
options.D: A dead pulsar emitting radio pulses

questions.explanation: Sir James Jeans describes our sun as a normal, medium-sized star among billions in the galactic heavens.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct grammatical error in the sentence: 'Neither of the boys have passed their examinations'?

options.A: 'Neither' is a singular indefinite pronoun and requires singular verbs ('has') and pronouns ('his').
options.B: 'Examinations' should be written in singular form.
options.C: 'Boys' should be replaced by 'students'.
options.D: 'Passed' should be 'passed through'.

questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb and pronoun: 'Neither of the boys has passed his examination.'

questions.question: What is the ultimate message of the first three essays in Book II?

options.A: To illustrate that human life is fragile, dependent on scientific understanding, and demands dedicated mental discipline to progress
options.B: To show that stars control human destiny through astrological alignments
options.C: To argue that college education is useless in the modern world
options.D: To prove that diseases cannot be prevented by sanitation

questions.explanation: These foundational essays examine cosmic context (Jeans), scientific enlightenment (Barnard & Edwards), and disciplined intellectual ambition (Hawkes).
